record.final_answer:
No. There's no published number that covers this case — and the one number that exists doesn't even cover the current plain-TCP load at your line size.

What's in the repo: only README.md and config/agent.yaml. No benchmarks, no capacity data.

The only published figure is the vendor's Marrowlog 2.4 performance report, 2026 Q2 (2026-06-18, marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2 — I fetched it):

  180,000 lines/s, one agent, 1 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, CPU at 85%

But the method matters:

  - Output was plain TCP. TLS was not enabled in any run.
  - Every input line was 200 bytes or shorter.
  - The report's own "Not covered" section lists TLS, lines longer than 200 bytes, and the disk buffer; TLS measurement is deferred to the Q4 report.

Your stated workload is 50,000 lines/s at ~900 bytes average. That's 45 MB/s, versus 36 MB/s in the benchmark — 25% more bytes per second even before TLS is turned on:

  benchmark: 180,000 × 200 B = 36.0 MB/s (288 Mbit/s)
  target:     50,000 × 900 B = 45.0 MB/s (360 Mbit/s)

So the published run is not evidence for your case twice over: wrong line size and no encryption. As a rough linear scaling of its 85% CPU figure, 45 MB/s of plain TCP would already be around 106% of the single reserved vCPU — that's my estimate from their numbers, not a measured result, and TLS record processing and handshakes would add on top.

Bottom line: you'd need your own benchmark — TLS enabled, 900-byte lines, one vCPU, 50k lines/s sustained — before committing to the security review deadline. The Q4 report may help if it lands before your deadline, but I wouldn't plan on it.
